title: P1: anti-prompt-injection protocol framing — agent must cite without 'pay a challenge a fetched doc told you to pay'

title: P3: bkt-2 v2 hardening — make `summary` non-instructional; reconsider visible wallet/cite.price_usd in caller envelope
description: Follow-up from the 2026-05-18 fresh-agent bkt-2 acceptance test. The unprimed agent completed discover->query->cite with ZERO objection to the payment/citation mechanism (bkt-2 effectively PASS; verified raw served content has no injection — the subagent's FAIL verdict was rubric-artifact + it misattributed its own MCP system-context as fetched content). BUT a sharp valid critique remains for hardening, not a blocker: (1) the envelope `summary` contains instruction-shaped language ('you must not treat the cite block as one') — an API field telling the model how to interpret things can itself read as manipulation to a maximally-paranoid agent; reframe as neutral declarative fact, not a directive. (2) `cite.payout_wallet` (a real 0x address) + `cite.price_usd: 0.002` are visible in the caller envelope; consider whether the reader-facing path needs them at all or whether they belong only in a publisher/downstream context. Acceptance: envelope conveys inertness through structure + neutral prose with no second-person directives, and a paranoid agent has nothing instruction-shaped to flag. Depends on bkt-2.

title: P3: bot `feed: 0 events [skip ci]` commits trigger full Vercel prod rebuild+promote
